clue.text: Team makes defensive moves to the wings

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
wards are guarding positions or parries in fencing

explanation.surface: A football team shifts its defenders out wide.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tactics on a pitch, but the wings here simply mean the sides, a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving towards the wings means moving laterally, towards one flank or other.

clue.text: Affray misrepresented in crime mags

indicators.note: presented wrongly, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A brawl reported inaccurately in crime magazines.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrimmage is a confused scuffle or brawl, as is an affray.

clue.text: Drank up in this storehouse

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily

explanation.surface: Someone drank up all the supplies in this warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TOPED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse or store.

clue.text: At such times as we have the right to embrace a bird

indicators.note: the shortened form of we have embraces the bird inside it

parts.note: we've is the contraction of we have
a hen is a bird
R is short for right

explanation.surface: Whenever we are entitled, we may hug a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts HEN inside WE'VE after its W, giving WHENEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means at any or every time that something happens.

clue.text: Turned to richer flights of eloquence

indicators.note: turned, as in twisted round, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker turned to ever richer flights of fine language.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive, ornate speech, full of high-flown passages.

clue.text: Contention in a way abounding

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
rife means widespread, abounding

explanation.surface: Arguments are everywhere on a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is conflict or disagreement.

clue.text: Tell target it's spotted in the middle

indicators.note: only the inner part of the word is kept, so its first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: dappled means marked with spots

explanation.surface: A remark about a bullseye that has a mark at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first and last letters of DAPPLED, the synonym for 'spotted'. William Tell, the Swiss folk hero, shot an arrow through a fruit on his son's head.
explanation.definitionFit: In the legend, the archer William Tell had to split a fruit balanced on his son's head.

clue.text: In this respect, a number get bogged down

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals
to mire is to sink or get stuck in a bog

explanation.surface: In this respect, several people are getting stuck in the mud.
explanation.walkthrough: D, Roman 500, stands for 'number'.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to hold them in high regard.

clue.text: Point Emma out in dumb-show

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Pointing Emma out using only mime.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime originally meant a show in mime, without words; in Britain it is also a comic Christmas stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumb-show is a performance in gesture alone, as mime was in the old sense.

clue.text: The introduction of electric light for each

indicators.note: the introduction is the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol

explanation.surface: Electric lighting being brought in for each home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like a lamp; it is a Very light, a military flare.
explanation.definitionFit: Every means each one of a group.

clue.text: Fully satisfied about point replayed in games lesson

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the replayed point goes inside the school sports lesson

parts.note: PE is physical education, the school games lesson
in tennis a let is a point that is played again

explanation.surface: Someone content after a tennis point is replayed during a school sports class.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means full up, completely satisfied after eating.

clue.text: The language of love?

parts.note: French, Italian and Spanish are ... languages, and French is often called the language of love; the word also means a love affair

explanation.surface: A question about the tongue spoken by lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a love affair and the group of tongues descended from Latin.

clue.text: Feet — just over three of them

definitions.meaning: poetic feet make up the rhythmic pattern of verse
the unit of length equals about 3.28 feet

explanation.surface: A measurement in feet, a little more than three.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the rhythmic pattern of verse built from feet and a length of roughly 3.3 feet.

clue.text: Collection of retired judge given to politician

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for judge is read backwards

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a game
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Gathering together the belongings of a former judge to hand them to a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns REF into FER. Collection here is the church collection taken during a service.
explanation.definitionFit: An offertory is the gathering of money from a congregation during a church service.

clue.text: Bill, a good character to send as an ambassador

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
credit is a good reputation

explanation.surface: A man named Bill is of sound reputation, fit to be posted abroad as a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is an account, abbreviated AC.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit an envoy is to give them official credentials to represent their country abroad.

clue.text: Tea dance

parts.note: cha is slang for tea, and the enumeration asks for it three times to name a Latin dance

explanation.surface: An afternoon social dance with tea.
explanation.walkthrough: A tea dance is a British afternoon social; here CHA (tea) three times gives a Latin American dance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a lively Latin American ballroom dance.

clue.text: The record is 600, roundabout

indicators.note: the Roman number goes round the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: DC is 600 in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A record number, 600, set at a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' looks like a road junction, but it tells you to put DC around IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record.

clue.text: Desert ship outside. Holyhead — a long time coming to the Lizard

indicators.note: the desert animal goes outside the letter, holding it

parts.note: the camel is called the ship of the desert
read as Holy head, the head or first letter of holy
an eon is an age, a very long time

explanation.surface: A ferry journey from the Welsh port of Holyhead, taking ages to reach the Cornish Lizard peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: Holyhead is a Welsh ferry port and the Lizard is a peninsula in Cornwall; both place names are hiding other meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon is a colour-changing reptile, a kind of lizard.

clue.text: Flier Jack in army support?

indicators.note: the sailor word goes inside the support word

parts.note: read as arm-y support: a sling supports an injured arm
jack tar, or tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Is a sailor serving in the army a kind of support?
explanation.walkthrough: 'army' must be read as arm-y: a support for the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A starling is a common bird, and so something that flies.

clue.text: Chick settling down

definitions.meaning: a young bird still in its nest
... also means snuggling or settling comfortably

explanation.surface: A baby bird settling down to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bird too young to leave the nest, and also the act of snuggling down comfortably.

clue.text: Cut back many a test .

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read from end to start

parts.note: to axe is to cut
M is a thousand in Roman numerals, so many

explanation.surface: Many tests are being cut back, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AXE into EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is an examination, a test of knowledge.

clue.text: … and the rest cut back, in fact excised

definitions.text: … and the rest cut back, in fact excised

parts.words: and the rest cut back, in fact excised
parts.note: the Latin phrase meaning and the rest is usually shortened to its first three letters, the remainder being cut out

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the remainder is cut back, in fact removed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on from 19 across. The full Latin phrase is normally cut back in writing to the abbreviation etc., its last five letters excised.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'and the other things', used at the end of a list.

clue.text: Such friends being more dear to us?

definitions.text: Such friends being more dear to us?

parts.words: Such friends being more dear to us?
parts.note: alludes to the saying that distance makes the heart grow fonder

explanation.surface: A wistful question about friends who are missed.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'absence makes the heart grow fonder' says people away from us become dearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends who are away from us are not present, and the proverb says we love them more.

clue.text: Emphasize Diana's out of danger

indicators.note: the short name is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: distress, as in a ship in distress, means danger
Di is short for Diana

explanation.surface: Stressing that Diana is now safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress something is to give it emphasis.

clue.text: I show how viciously I hit boxer

indicators.note: the fierce, uncontrolled blow suggests the letters flying into a new order

explanation.surface: A boxer explains how fiercely he lands a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viciously' rearranges I HIT BOXER. The definition is what the person would say about themselves: 'I show'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibitor is someone who puts things on display, at a show or gallery.

clue.text: Record some (not all) races here

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: not all of the word is used, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Recording some of the races held here.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom, in Surrey, is the English racecourse where the Derby is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a famous racecourse, home of the Derby.

clue.text: What a stew appears to have and does

definitions.text: What a stew appears to have

definitions.meaning: the verb sense: the stew has a flavour of something

explanation.surface: A stew seems to have flavour and indeed it does.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is flavour; as a verb it means to have a flavour, as a stew does.

clue.text: Pan on the housetop

definitions.meaning: to pan is to criticise harshly
a roofing tile of grey stone

explanation.surface: A cooking pan left up on the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate a play is to criticise it severely, and slates are the stone tiles covering a roof.

clue.text: Use non-U island as hideaway?

indicators.note: non-U says take away the letter U from the word before

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Using an island somewhere other than the U as a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' is also British slang for socially unrefined, which the surface plays on. USE without U leaves SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to hide it away.

clue.text: Ape has one officer holding it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the officer word holds the other word inside it

parts.note: a mate is an officer on a merchant ship
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ape with a ship's officer who is holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy or mimic them.

clue.text: Imported beef, perhaps, with name concealed

indicators.note: the abbreviation is concealed within the food word

parts.note: beef is an example of meat

explanation.surface: Beef brought in from abroad with its name hidden on the label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imported' looks like brought in from abroad, but here it means signified: to import is to mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Import can mean signify, so imported is a synonym of signified.

clue.text: A shade immature to follow pundit's lead

indicators.note: the word for immature comes after the pundit word in the answer

parts.note: a sage is a wise pundit; lead says it goes first
green means inexperienced, immature

explanation.surface: A young novice copying the example of an expert commentator.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a soft greyish-green colour, like the herb's leaves.
